headline: A halted weekend tape carries a just-hiked Fed, a 4.998% 10-year and ~$100 crude into an unpriced Sunday reopen, with Tail pinned at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly eight hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this assessment: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5.1bp to 4.998% after topping 5.00% earlier in the week for the first time since 2023, against a 2-year of 4.67% on the September 17 H.15. WTI traded near $100 and Brent near $103 after a third consecutive decline, and December gold settled at $4,420.45. The backdrop is genuinely tense. The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16, its first increase since 2023, by unanimous vote, with 16 of 18 participants projecting a further hike this year and the statement citing elevated inflation driven in part by energy costs. A drone attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline, the route built to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, has left Riyadh signalling half capacity within days and a full repair in roughly six weeks while barrels are rerouted by sea. Reported consideration of renewed strikes on Iran ahead of a Gulf leaders meeting in New York is an open geopolitical checkpoint, and the unresolved AI-safety debate remains a tech-specific narrative risk. None of that changes the Tail assessment for this window. Tail measures a price path that denies mean reversion, and a halted market has no mechanism to produce one. Friday's session was rotational rather than one-way, with semiconductors and AI hardware bid while software, IBM and the Dow cyclicals lagged, and it closed with volatility at the low of its range. Tail therefore holds 5 and eases to 4 through the deepest stretch of the halt, lifting only to 6 late on Sunday as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates ahead of a reopen that lies outside this window. Stress drifts from 22 to 29, crossing into the moderate band on elapsed unpriced time rather than on any new stress event, and Confidence steps from 75 to 65 as verified Friday evidence ages with nothing able to refresh it.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed U.S. cash session, eased to 16 into the close, then fell through 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final fifteen slots. Stress peaked at 51 in the Friday afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive hours before settling at 22. Confidence held between 75 and 88, easing steadily once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode was mixed across the cash session, turned trend-up into the close and has read normal for every hour since the weekend halt began.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly eight hours after the final slot here. Tail holds 5 for three hours, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 10:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Those steps reflect proximity and unpriced elapsed time, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 22 to 29, crossing into the moderate band at 04:00Z Sunday on staleness alone, and Confidence steps from 75 to 65 as Friday's verified evidence ages. Energy and Middle East headlines are the most plausible weekend surprise vector, with the Saudi pipeline repair timeline and reported consideration of renewed Iran strikes the named checkpoints; any such development would raise Stress and reopen-gap risk first, and would reach Tail only if a reopened tape genuinely refused retracement.
